## Flamingo, Costa Rica: sea fishing and relaxation by the Pacific

Flamingo lies on the northwestern Pacific coast of [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/), in Guanacaste Province. The area is known for offshore fishing trips and coastal boat routes. Fishing grounds differ in depth, distance from shore, and fish species. Before choosing an itinerary, decide whether you want a full day on a boat, several consecutive fishing days, or a mix of fishing and time on land.

Flamingo is also a resort area with beaches and access to marine facilities. For some travelers it is the starting point of a fishing expedition; for others, it is a single active day within a longer journey through Costa Rica.

## Two kinds of sea fishing near Flamingo

**Offshore fishing in the deeper Pacific** targets pelagic species moving through open water. Possible catches mentioned in our itineraries for this area include sailfish; blue, black, and striped marlin; mahi-mahi; and yellowfin and bigeye tuna. These are species found in the area, not a promise of a catch.

**Fishing near the islands and coastal areas** takes place in different conditions. Our itineraries mention the Catalina and Brummel islands, as well as wahoo, mackerel, several kinds of snapper or grouper, and roosterfish. Even when boats depart from the same area, depth, weather, and suitable tackle may vary considerably between the two types of fishing.

| Format | Key feature |
|---|---|
| Open ocean | Pelagic species, longer boat trips |
| Island waters | Different depths and tackle |

The day's actual route depends on the forecast, safety, trip duration, and the crew's professional judgment. Discuss your preferred format before booking, particularly if some travelers have never been sea fishing.

## Which Ada Tours itineraries include Flamingo?

The [seven-day “Fishing in Costa Rica” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-fishing/) devotes several days to fishing at sea. It begins with arrival in San José and a transfer to the Pacific coast, with most of the journey spent around Flamingo. This suits travelers for whom fishing is the main goal and the number of boat outings matters more than visiting many national parks.

Flamingo plays a different role on the [13-day “Extreme Costa Rica” itinerary](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/). The route combines natural areas, rafting on the Pacuare River, Arenal, and Monteverde. Near the end, there is a dedicated day of sport fishing around Flamingo, followed by diving near the Catalina Islands. This option suits travelers interested in varied activities, with fishing as one part of a busy journey.

These are **two different products**, and the tour you choose determines the actual fishing days, meals, accommodation, and included services. Fishing appearing on both itineraries does not mean they have the same number of boat trips, daily arrangements, or price.

## What to arrange before going out on the boat

For a day at sea, agree in advance on the meeting time, trip duration, number of participants, boat type, provided equipment, and what happens in bad weather. Check whether tackle, bait, meals, drinks, and crew services are included in your particular offer. Equipment being available from local operators does not itself mean it is included in a specific tour.

**Seasickness** can spoil an otherwise enjoyable outing. Travelers sensitive to boat motion should discuss a calmer format and appropriate precautions with a doctor in advance. On board, protect yourself from sun and wind, wear shoes with non-slip soles, and bring enough water. The captain's instructions and safety rules apply regardless of fishing experience.

For sport fishing, pay attention to local requirements for permits, handling catches, and releasing fish. Rules vary by species and current regulations; do not assume that every caught fish may be kept.

## Fishing seasons and ocean conditions

Sea fishing takes place off Guanacaste in different months, but the presence of particular species, wind, swell, and the frequency of successful outings change through the year. The relatively dry season on the Pacific coast generally runs from December to April. This is a useful guide when planning a holiday, but does not guarantee calm seas or a particular catch.

When choosing dates, first identify the species or style of fishing that interests you, then consider the season and likely access to the grounds on your preferred days. We help match that goal with an actual itinerary and a suitable number of nights on the coast.

## Flamingo without fishing: other options

The area's beaches and bays also offer time for ordinary relaxation by the ocean. Flamingo is part of the same broad Guanacaste coastal region as [Playa Conchal](/costa-rica/place/playa-conchal/), known for its shell-covered shore, and [Tamarindo](/costa-rica/place/playa-tamarindo/), with surfing and resort cafés. These are distinct places: one may be better for a relaxed beach day, another for surf lessons, and Flamingo for boating and fishing.

If your group has varied interests, a fishing day can be planned for those who want it, while others spend time ashore. Specific transfers, activities, and conditions must be agreed for the particular journey. For more options, explore [fishing tours](/interests/fishing/) and the [Costa Rica travel catalog](/costa-rica/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about Flamingo

### Can I catch a marlin on a trip to Flamingo?

Marlin inhabit waters reached by fishing boats departing from Flamingo. However, spotting and catching one depend on the season, weather, and luck; neither can be guaranteed.

### Is one day or several days better for a first offshore fishing trip?

A single day is a convenient introduction. Several trips provide more opportunities to find suitable conditions and try different grounds, but require more time on the coast. Consider your tolerance for boat motion and the other aims of your journey.

### Is Flamingo suitable for travelers who do not fish?

Yes. It is also a beach and resort area, with other Guanacaste beaches nearby. Check whether any particular visits are actually included in your chosen tour.

## Which Ada Tours itineraries include Flamingo?

There are {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} passing through [Flamingo](/costa-rica/place/flamingo/). This area of Costa Rica's northwestern Pacific coast is a departure point for sea fishing. However, the two established itineraries have different aims: fishing takes up most of one journey, while it is just one of several active days on the other.

[“Fishing in Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-fishing/) is a specialized **seven-day** itinerary. After arriving in San José, travelers transfer to the Pacific coast and spend several of the following days fishing near Flamingo.

[“Extreme Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) is a **13-day** itinerary featuring rafting on the Pacuare River, canyoning near Arenal, activities in Monteverde, and time on the coast. Fishing near Flamingo takes place on day 10, followed by diving near the Catalina Islands on the next day.

| Itinerary | Main goal |
|---|---|
| [Fishing, 7 days](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-fishing/) | Several days of sea fishing |
| [Extreme Adventure, 13 days](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) | Varied adventures and one fishing day |

The duration and price of the current programs are best compared in their own tour listings:

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_pybalka_v_kosta_rike,tour_source_ekstrim_v_kosta_rike}}

## Specialized fishing trip: several days on the water

On the seven-day tour, the main fishing grounds are near Flamingo. The itinerary begins with arrival in San José and a transfer to the Pacific coast. Days 3 through 6 are then devoted to fishing, with the final day reserved for the return journey to the airport.

Our program identifies two distinct fishing areas.

**Open ocean.** Approximately 20 miles west of Flamingo harbor, the seabed drops away rapidly. Large pelagic fish that may be found here include sailfish, several types of marlin, mahi-mahi, yellowfin tuna, and bigeye tuna.

**Island waters.** Closer to the [Catalina Islands](/costa-rica/place/catalina-islands/) and Brummel, about five miles from the harbor, the itinerary mentions wahoo, mackerel, horse mackerel, snapper or grouper, and roosterfish.

Offshore and nearshore fishing offer different experiences. In the first, the boat journey to the fishing grounds and handling large ocean fish are especially important. In the second, the depths, species, and search conditions change. Results depend on season, weather, sea conditions, and luck; listing a species in the itinerary does not guarantee a catch.

The tour specifies accommodation near [Playa Tamarindo](/costa-rica/place/playa-tamarindo/), while fishing days are based around Flamingo. This matters when selecting an itinerary: the place where you stay overnight may differ from the point where you depart to fish.

## Extreme Costa Rica: fishing as part of an adventure

The second option is for travelers who want to experience the country's nature through different activities. Before reaching Flamingo, the itinerary passes through [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), the [Pacuare River](/costa-rica/place/pacuare-river/), [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), and the Pacific coast.

**Day 10** features sport fishing near Flamingo. The program mentions both deep-water grounds west of the harbor and island areas closer to Catalina. **Day 11** brings a different main activity: [diving near the Catalina Islands](/costa-rica/place/catalina-islands/), taking the participant's experience and diving conditions into account.

This is a good choice if you want to try sea fishing without devoting nearly the whole trip to it. The 13-day option also includes physically demanding activities, such as rafting, waterfall descents, quad biking, and other pursuits. Assess the complete itinerary against your abilities, rather than judging it by one day at sea.

It is important to distinguish **fishing from diving**. They may take place in nearby marine areas, but they require different preparation and equipment. For diving-focused options, see the [Costa Rica diving tour catalog](/interests/diving/tours/costa-rica/).

## What kinds of fishing are available near Flamingo?

Costa Rica's northwestern Pacific coast is known for sport fishing at sea. When selecting an itinerary, it is more useful to consider the fishing style and duration than promises of landing a particular fish.

**Pelagic fish** include sailfish, marlin, mahi-mahi, and tuna. Fishing for them takes you into deeper ocean waters. The length of the boat trip and weather conditions are particularly relevant.

**Fishing closer to islands and reefs** may target roosterfish, wahoo, mackerel, and other species mentioned in our programs. Being close to islands does not automatically mean calm water: wind, waves, and currents influence decisions about whether to go out and where to fish.

If fishing is your primary passion, consider [specialized fishing tours](/interests/fishing/tours/costa-rica/). If you would rather combine the ocean with volcanoes, rivers, and forests, compare the full [Costa Rica tour catalog](/costa-rica/tour/).

## Season, sea conditions, and preparation

Guanacaste's Pacific coast has a relatively dry period from approximately December through April and wetter months from May through November. But **the best season for a beach holiday and a suitable day for fishing are different criteria**. Wind and strong waves can occur even in the dry season, while some trips during rainy months can be successful.

When planning, consider how you feel at sea, travel time on the boat, your preferred fishing style, and flexibility of the schedule. For large ocean fish, the number of available fishing days is especially important: the dedicated seven-day tour has several, while Flamingo occupies only one day of the 13-day adventure.

Sport fishing is regulated in Costa Rica. INCOPESCA describes requirements for fishing licenses and permits; check the precise application process and relevant rules for your date and fishing method. **Do not assume from a tour's name that every license, piece of tackle, or fee is included in the price.** The confirmed services are listed on the selected tour's page.

## Choosing the right itinerary

Choose the [seven-day fishing itinerary](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-fishing/) if you want several trips out to sea and a focus on fishing. The 13-day option is more suitable if fishing appeals to you alongside rafting, canyoning, a visit to Arenal, and diving.

In both cases, Flamingo is part of [Costa Rica's Pacific coast](/costa-rica/place/pacific-coast/). Consider not only the overall trip duration and price, but also **the number of fishing days**, other required activities, the hotel's location, and the level of physical fitness needed. Read the actual itinerary to check which boat outings are planned, which services are included, and what depends on sea conditions.

## Questions about tours passing through Flamingo

### Which tour should I choose if sea fishing is my main goal?

The seven-day [“Fishing in Costa Rica” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-fishing/). Several consecutive days are devoted to fishing near Flamingo, giving travelers more opportunities to focus on this activity.

### Is there a tour combining fishing with active adventures?

Yes. The 13-day [“Extreme Costa Rica” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) combines rafting, canyoning, volcanic regions, fishing near Flamingo, and diving at Catalina.

### On which day of the extreme tour does fishing take place?

On day 10. The following day includes diving near the Catalina Islands, for which appropriate experience is needed.

### Which fish can be found near Flamingo?

The itineraries mention sailfish, marlin, mahi-mahi, tuna, wahoo, mackerel, and roosterfish. The potential catch depends on the fishing grounds, season, and actual conditions. Catching any particular species cannot be guaranteed.

### Can I fish near Flamingo without going diving?

Yes. The specialized [seven-day fishing tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-fishing/) focuses on fishing and does not require purchasing a separate diving program.

### Are special documents required for sport fishing?

INCOPESCA regulates sport-fishing licenses and permits. Before traveling, check the requirements for tourists and your particular fishing method; do not assume how they will be obtained or paid for.

### Does visiting Flamingo mean staying overnight in the town itself?

No. For example, on the seven-day itinerary, the fishing area is near Flamingo, but coastal accommodation is specified at Tamarindo Diria. Compare the fishing base and hotel location separately.

## Places to visit in Costa Rica: national parks, volcanoes, and two ocean coasts

Costa Rica attracts travelers for its natural areas: volcanic scenery, cloud forests, birds and wildlife, rivers, and coastlines. This catalog brings together cities, parks, islands, and regions from which you can build an itinerary. Separate pages are available for [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/), [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), and other destinations.

To plan a rewarding journey, decide on the main priority: seeing as many national parks as possible or allowing enough days to relax by the sea. Even in a relatively compact country, transfers between coasts, mountain forests, and volcanoes take time.

## Which natural regions should you choose?

| Region | Main attractions |
|---|---|
| Arenal and La Fortuna | Volcano and hot springs |
| Monteverde | Cloud forest and birds |
| Manuel Antonio | Forest and Pacific beaches |
| Osa and Corcovado | Tropical nature |
| Tortuguero | Canals and sea turtles |
| Poás | Volcanic crater |

### Arenal, La Fortuna, and Poás

[La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) make a convenient base for a nature-focused itinerary with walking excursions and hot springs. Spending several nights here avoids squeezing every outing into a single day. Moisture and clouds sometimes obscure the summit, so avoid choosing the area solely for a supposedly guaranteed view of the volcano.

[Poás Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/) is known for its crater scenery. It is an active volcano, and park management regulates access to viewing areas for safety reasons. A visit may be combined with [La Paz Waterfalls](/costa-rica/place/la-paz-waterfalls/), but the actual order and timing depend on the itinerary.

### Monteverde: cloud forests and nocturnal nature

[Monteverde and Santa Elena](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) are characterized by humid forests, mosses, and epiphytes. They are ideal for walking trails and birdwatching. The famous quetzal inhabits this ecosystem, but a sighting on any particular day cannot be guaranteed.

Monteverde suits nature photographers and travelers who enjoy unhurried walks, though forest trails can be slippery. Closed-toe shoes and a waterproof jacket are advisable. Activities such as hanging bridges or zip-lining should be selected separately according to operator availability and age restrictions.

### Manuel Antonio and the Pacific coast

At [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/), tropical forest meets the sea. It is easier to combine park walks with a beach day here than to undertake separate long transfers for each type of experience. The national park has entry rules and wildlife protections: feeding wild monkeys and other animals is prohibited.

Different beach experiences are available at [Tamarindo](/costa-rica/place/playa-tamarindo/), [Montezuma](/costa-rica/place/montezuma/), and [Playa Conchal](/costa-rica/place/playa-conchal/). Waves, the seabed, and opportunities for water sports vary along the Pacific coast. For family outings or surfing, choose a beach to fit your specific needs rather than treating every part of the coast as the same.

### Corcovado and the Osa Peninsula

The [Osa Peninsula](/costa-rica/place/osa-peninsula/) and [Corcovado National Park](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/) suit travelers prepared to devote more time to nature. This tropical region has rich wildlife, and walks follow the rules of protected parkland. Check access, guide requirements, and seasonal restrictions before traveling.

Nearby are [Drake Bay](/costa-rica/place/drake-bay/) and marine destinations. When choosing an itinerary, distinguish land-based park walks from separate activities at sea, including those around [Caño Island](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/). They require different arrangements and may depend on marine weather.

### Tortuguero and the Caribbean coast

[Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/) is known for its canal network and coastal forests. It is a destination for boat excursions and wildlife observation. Sea turtles come ashore during particular seasons, and visits to nesting areas are governed by specific rules. These should not be treated as ordinary unrestricted beach attractions.

[Puerto Viejo](/costa-rica/place/puerto-viejo/) and [Puerto Limón](/costa-rica/place/puerto-limon/) offer another side of the Caribbean coast: local culture, tropical scenery, and the sea. Rainfall patterns on the Caribbean side can differ from those on Costa Rica's Pacific coast.

## Combining destinations into one itinerary

For an introduction to Costa Rica, combine **Arenal, Monteverde, and Manuel Antonio**: three different ecosystems, each worthy of a separate stop. If wildlife observation is your primary interest, consider adding Corcovado or Tortuguero, allowing enough time for more complex logistics.

December through April is generally drier across much of the Pacific coast, with more frequent rain from May through November. This is a broad guideline; conditions on the Caribbean coast and in cloud forests may differ. When planning, check trail availability, admission rules, and current national park restrictions.

Explore ready-made itineraries in the [Costa Rica tour catalog](/costa-rica/tour/). For more on geography, climate, and holiday formats, visit our [Costa Rica page](/costa-rica/).

## Frequently asked questions about places to visit in Costa Rica

### Where is best for wildlife viewing?

Manuel Antonio, Corcovado, Monteverde, and Tortuguero all offer nature walks, but sightings of specific species are not guaranteed.

### What should I choose for a first visit?

Arenal, Monteverde, and one Pacific coastal area often make a convenient combination, providing volcanic landscapes, cloud forest, and the ocean.

### Can Poás crater be visited on any day?

No. Entry and access to viewing areas depend on volcanic activity and park management decisions.

### Where can I find surfing beaches?

Compare Tamarindo and other Pacific resorts by season, wave conditions, and your experience. Some beaches are more suitable for swimming; others are better for surfing.

## Jacó, Costa Rica: beaches, surfing, and independent nature excursions

Jacó is on the central Pacific coast of [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/). The resort has a long strip of dark sand, noticeable surf, and well-developed town facilities. It is easy to combine surfing lessons, walks by the ocean, restaurants, and excursions outside town. Jacó is particularly convenient for travelers who want to begin their trip on the coast after arriving in the San José area.

The main distinction between Jacó and quiet beach coves is the style of holiday. The ocean is often energetic here: strong currents and breaking waves call for attention, while nearby shops, surf schools, and evening venues make the resort lively. Choose Jacó primarily for surfing and as a convenient base for outings, rather than for guaranteed calm water.

## Jacó Beach and where to surf

The main beach extends for about 4 km between coastal hills. This broad, open stretch makes the tide, breaking waves, and changing sea conditions easy to observe. To walk on the sand, you only need to reach the shore; getting into the water calls for attention to the precise section, weather, and current waves.

Jacó is a major surfing center on the central Pacific coast. Beginners should start with an instructor who chooses the location according to the group's skills, surf strength, and currents. Going out on a board simply because other surfers are nearby is unwise: conditions can differ even between neighboring stretches of beach.

Experienced surfers may also be interested in the wider Pacific area, including Playa Hermosa. However, waves suited to a skilled surfer can be dangerous for a first lesson. The right time and conditions for each surf spot should be determined locally.

## Is swimming in Jacó safe?

Swimming is possible only when current conditions allow it. Costa Rica's official tourism pages specifically note **strong currents near Jacó**. A long beach does not offer the same level of safety along its entire length. Take special care after rain, during heavy surf, and on unfamiliar stretches of shoreline.

Follow recommendations from local lifeguards and instructors, pay attention to warnings, do not swim far out, and do not confuse a surf-training area with a safe swimming zone. For a trip with small children or a focus on relaxed swimming, compare Jacó with [Playa Conchal](/costa-rica/place/playa-conchal/), where the coast is different, although sea conditions still change from day to day.

## Things to do beyond the beach

Jacó is a useful base for trips into the natural areas of the central Pacific coast. North of the resort is the Tárcoles River area, known for crocodiles and boat excursions. Observe animals from a safe distance and follow the rules of your chosen outing. Wild animals do not become safe to approach merely because tourists often see them.

Another possible excursion is Carara National Park, home to several types of tropical forest and numerous birds. Before visiting, check current trail access, opening hours, and suitable walking conditions. It is better to set aside part of a day for a nature outing than to cram it between several consecutive surfing activities.

Jacó itself has plenty of cafés, restaurants, and small shops for an evening after the beach. If a quiet night's sleep is important, choose accommodation with its distance from bars and nightlife streets in mind.

## How long to stay and where Jacó fits into a trip

For a first introduction, **2–3 days** is often a useful planning guideline: one day for arrival and a walk, another for surfing, and perhaps a separate nature excursion. This is advice about pacing, not a fixed Ada Tours itinerary. Allow more time for several full surfing lessons or rest between active experiences.

Jacó combines conveniently with [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/), as it lies relatively close to central Costa Rica by road. Actual driving time depends on the route, traffic, and departure point. If you want to visit national parks after time at the ocean, compare available itineraries by duration and stops in the [Costa Rica tour catalog](/costa-rica/tour/). Simply staying in Jacó does not mean the resort is included in every catalog itinerary.

## Jacó versus the beaches of Guanacaste

| Resort | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Jacó | Surfing and town life |
| [Tamarindo](/costa-rica/place/playa-tamarindo/) | Beach and surf schools |
| [Playa Conchal](/costa-rica/place/playa-conchal/) | Light-colored shell-covered shore |
| [Flamingo](/costa-rica/place/flamingo/) | Boat outings and fishing |

These coastal areas lie in different parts of the country. The right choice depends on how many days you have and whether a separate drive north is worthwhile. For a short beach segment, staying in one area can make more sense than transferring daily between several resorts.

## When to visit and what to bring

On the Pacific coast, the drier months generally fall between December and April, while May through November bring more frequent rain. However, whether a particular day is good for surfing depends on sea conditions, wave direction, and wind, so there is no single “perfect month” for all skill levels.

For walks, bring sun protection, lightweight clothing, water, and comfortable shoes. For surfing, check board rental terms, insurance, age restrictions, and lesson requirements before entering the water. We help fit a resort stay into a broader journey and leave enough time for transfers.

## Frequently asked questions about Jacó

### Is Jacó suitable for a first surfing lesson?

Yes. Jacó has surfing facilities, but it is best to take your first session with an instructor, who will select a place and time suited to the actual waves and the participant's skills.

### Can I choose Jacó just for swimming at the beach?

You can spend beach days here, but strong currents make Jacó less predictable for relaxed swimming. For that kind of holiday, compare coves in other coastal areas.

### Is it easy to combine Jacó with nature excursions?

Yes. The central Pacific coast offers separate excursions to the Tárcoles River and Carara National Park. Check availability for your specific travel dates.

## La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano: what to see in Costa Rica

La Fortuna in northern [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/) is known for the almost perfectly conical Arenal Volcano. The volcano is visible from many parts of the valley, but there is much more to explore than one viewpoint. The area also has tropical forest, volcanic rock, a waterfall, a large lake, and thermal pools.

For a well-planned itinerary, distinguish between **Arenal Volcano National Park**, privately operated hanging-bridge parks, La Fortuna Waterfall, and hot-spring areas. They belong to the same wider destination but have separate entrances, tickets, and visiting times.

## Arenal Volcano: what is happening now?

Arenal became famous for a period of intense volcanic activity that began in 1968. For decades, travelers came to see glowing lava and ash clouds. However, **regular lava eruptions stopped around 2010**. Scientific and conservation materials describe the volcano's present phase as relatively calm.

Do not expect to see molten lava flowing down the slopes. Today's main sights are the volcanic cone itself, old hardened lava flows, vegetation returning to previously disturbed ground, and views over the lake.

Thick clouds sometimes conceal the summit. To improve your chances of a clear view, allow some flexibility rather than planning a single short stop at a fixed hour.

## What to see in Arenal National Park

In [Arenal Volcano National Park](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), the SINAC conservation authority describes several walking trails. The **Coladas** trail passes old lava deposits and leads to views of the volcano, lake, and Tilarán mountains. **El Ceibo** leads through forest to an old, large ceiba tree. **Heliconias** offers a shorter walk among the vegetation.

These trails vary in length and difficulty. Choose according to the weather, trail conditions, and your fitness. Follow park markings, do not enter closed areas on the volcanic slopes, and check access conditions with SINAC.

Viewpoints are particularly appealing for those who want to see the boundary between dark volcanic rock and green vegetation.

## Hanging bridges, the waterfall, and hot springs

The La Fortuna area offers several distinct experiences:

- **Hanging bridges:** walking above the humid forest lets you observe the treetops and look for birds.
- **La Fortuna Waterfall:** known for a tall cascade surrounded by tropical greenery; access requires descending and then climbing steps.
- **Hot springs:** the warm water is related to the area's geothermal activity, and the experience depends on the particular complex.
- **Lake Arenal:** views of the water and volcano, with separate water-based activities at certain locations.

Do not try to fit all these places into just a few hours. For a relaxed forest walk, unhurried rest, and good photographs, allocate different parts of the day or stay several nights in the area.

## La Fortuna on Ada Tours itineraries

On the [Costa Rica: Arenal, San José, and the Pacific Ocean tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-3-perspectives/), you leave San José for the Arenal area. On **day three**, you walk across the hanging bridges at Mistico Park and continue exploring the volcanic region.

Compare this option with other [Costa Rica tours](/costa-rica/tour/). Arenal is the main nature destination on some itineraries and just one stop en route to Monteverde or the coast on others. Choose by the activities actually listed, not just the volcano's name.

## How long to stay and when to go

La Fortuna lies in a rainy tropical zone. Heavy showers are possible even in months considered relatively dry elsewhere in Costa Rica. Pack a light rain jacket, non-slip shoes, and a dry case for your phone or camera.

One full day allows you to choose the national park and one other activity. With two days, it is easier to combine forest walks, the waterfall, and hot springs without turning your trip into a series of hurried transfers.

## Frequently asked questions about La Fortuna and Arenal

### Can visitors see lava erupting at Arenal today?

The volcano is in a relatively calm phase. The regular lava activity for which it became famous after 1968 ended around 2010. Tourist trails mainly reveal older lava formations and natural landscapes.

### Are Arenal Volcano and La Fortuna Waterfall the same attraction?

No. They are separate attractions in the same area, with different routes and visiting conditions.

### Does Ada Tours offer hanging bridges on an itinerary?

Yes. For example, the [“Arenal, San José, and Beach Holiday” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-3-perspectives/) includes a day walking on the Mistico hanging bridges.

### Where should I stay to explore the Arenal area?

La Fortuna is a convenient base for trips to the volcano, waterfall, and hot springs. The exact accommodation depends on the tour you choose.
